headline: Latent models recover spatial cell states and niche programs from transcriptomic data
label: Spatial Omics Latent Models
summary: Recent preprints pair learned latent representations with spatial transcriptomics, 3D reconstruction and causal or lineage-aware modelling.
synthesis: The common thread is learned latent structure over spatially resolved transcriptomic data, where models aim to separate intrinsic cell states from tissue context. GaLF-ST places expression on learnable Gaussian latent fields with a shared decoder and benchmarks reconstruction against comparator methods. CIRCA applies self-supervised causal representation learning to recover identifiable cell- and niche-level programs and their interactions with tissue pathology. SOUR decomposes spatial lineage tracing data into heritable lineage and microenvironmental effects on tumor gene expression. A rotation-equivariant network reconstructs 3D cell shape from transcript point clouds, and CASTLE uses contrastive graph learning with cell-type-aware spatial graphs for spatial domain detection. The hybrid mixture of factor analyzers is non-spatial and serves as a probabilistic alternative rather than a spatial method. What is new is the shift from descriptive embeddings toward identifiable, context-separated representations.
